verdict.rationale: FFmpeg is itself an official command-line tool. Its first-party docs at ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg.html give worked examples covering inputs, bitrate, frame rate, stream mapping and filtergraphs, and community users confirm heavy hands-on CLI use, including having LLMs generate commands. missing for 10: evidence of agent-oriented CLI features such as machine-readable/structured output, plus users' reports that the syntax is opaque, the docs terse, and shell escaping painful.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: The ffmpeg CLI tool can configure IAMF structure with the new -stream_group option.
Set the video bitrate of the output file to 64 kbit/s: ffmpeg -i input.avi -b:v 64k -bufsize 64k output.mp4
